explanations.answer: All the days of Jehoiada the priest
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. The text says Joash did what was right “…all the days of Jehoiada the priest.” That's Jehoiada, the priest who crowned him (2 Chronicles 23:11). I think a young king leaned on that man a lot.

explanations.answer: All forty years of his reign
explanations.explanation: Forty years is how long Joash reigned, and that's in verse 1. But this verse measures his right-doing on a different clock: “…all the days of Jehoiada the priest.” That's the time the text names here. Two clocks, friend, and this verse is reading the Jehoiada one.

explanations.answer: Only for his first seven years

The leftovers went right back into the LORD's house.

explanations.answer: He did what was good in Israel for God and His temple
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The text says Jehoiada “…was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done what was good in Israel for God and His temple.” Jehoiada is called the high priest in verse 6, and still he was buried with the kings. The text gives the reason right there in the verse.

explanations.answer: He ruled Judah as king while Joash was young
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that, friend. It says Jehoiada “…was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done what was good in Israel for God and His temple.” Jehoiada was a priest who served beside the king. The reason given is the good he did for God and His temple.

explanations.answer: He led Judah's army to a great victory in battle
explanations.explanation: No battle appears in this passage, baker. The text says Jehoiada “…was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done what was good in Israel for God and His temple.” Jehoiada was a priest, and his good was done for God and His temple.
